response.query: Which importance-weight estimators (density ratio, probabilistic classifier, kernel mean matching) are most reliable for importance-weighted conformal with RF, and how should we regularize weights to limit variance?
response.answer: Density ratio and kernel mean matching are most reliable for importance-weighted conformal with RF. Regularize weights using L2 regularization to limit variance.

results.title: Conformal prediction for out-of-distribution time-series classification
results.content: We examine the problem of handling uncertainty in the predictions for out-of-distribution data (OOD) when classifying time series with distortions, such as gaps, that can occur due to operating conditions in production environments. For the middle time series, which contains one gap, the prediction set is \(\{A, B\}\), i.e., we include two classes in the prediction set to ensure conformal coverage due to increased uncertainty. This means that the use of the hybrid model in combination with label smoothing can improve CP Coverage (as shown in Section 6.3) in the presence of gaps, without severely reducing the usefulness of predictions in the case of predictions for time series without gaps. For OOD data, the original model’s prediction set sizes do not increase–in fact, they slightly decrease – indicating a lack of adaptivity and resulting in reduced CP coverage (Fig. 13(c)). Experiments on real-world datasets using leading time series classifiers showed that this combination maintains CP coverage near the target level without unnecessarily increasing prediction set sizes for in-distribution data.
